entities.name: Group of States Against Corruption
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Group of States Against Corruption (GRECO) serves as an essential monitoring body established in 1999 under the auspices of the Council of Europe, headquartered in the Palace of Europe in Strasbourg, France. Its formation was a direct response to the growing recognition of corruption as a pervasive threat to democratic governance, economic stability, and social justice across Europe and beyond. GRECO's mission is to enhance the capacity of its member states to combat corruption through a rigorous peer-review mechanism and compliance assessments. This body comprises 50 member states, including all 47 Council of Europe member states and the United States, underlining its significance in global anti-corruption efforts.

Since its inception, GRECO has conducted numerous evaluations, producing over 20 rounds of reports assessing the anti-corruption measures of its member states. These evaluations cover various domains, including the judiciary, law enforcement, and public officials' conduct, leading to tangible improvements in national laws and practices. For instance, in its 2018 evaluation cycle, GRECO highlighted the need for enhanced transparency in political financing, which resulted in legislative reforms in several countries, demonstrating the organization's impactful oversight.

The legacy of GRECO lies in its contribution to the international discourse on corruption and governance, shaping how member states approach anti-corruption strategies. As a result of GRECO's influence, many countries have adopted best practices and strengthened legal frameworks. Furthermore, GRECO's reports have become key references for civil society organizations and watchdogs, illustrating the interdependence of global governance and accountability mechanisms.
